items.heading: Physiotherapy Is a Real, Regulated,
items.text: Physiotherapy is a real, regulated, growing clinical career in India, not a dressed-up fitness job with no ceiling. But "is physiotherapy good" and "will the first few years feel good on your body" are two different questions, and most course brochures blur them together until you cannot tell which one is actually being answered.

items.heading: Here Is the Part Most
items.text: Here is the part most "physiotherapy scope" pages soften. The brochure version of this career and the version a fresh BPT graduate actually lives through in year one are describing two different jobs, and the gap between them is the real source of the field's underreported injury and attrition problem.

items.heading: "Physiotherapy Salary in India"
items.text: "Physiotherapy salary in India" is close to a meaningless single number, because the spread between a first-year clinic trainee and an established private-practice owner is enormous, and most college marketing quotes only the flattering end of it.

items.heading: Course Brochures Lean
items.text: Course brochures lean on the "healer," "sports-team physio," and "help people walk again" framing, the emotionally satisfying version of the job that pulls PCB students toward BPT every admission season.

items.heading: Placement
items.text: Placement-day stories about the rare graduate who joins an IPL franchise or an international sports academy circulate widely, while the far more common first job, a private-clinic trainee role on modest pay, barely gets mentioned.
